title: Closing a conversation runtime leaves event listeners registered
reasoning: SdkConversationRuntime tracks both snapshot listeners and event listeners, but close() only clears snapshot listeners. Any callbacks registered through subscribeEvents(), WindieChatSession.onEvent(), or stream-adjacent consumers remain retained after close. If an in-flight send, stop, rewrite, or tool execution applies another event after close, notify() still invokes those closed-session event callbacks and the Set continues to retain captured UI/session state.
recommendation: Have close() also clear eventListeners, and consider making apply/notify paths no-op after close if closed runtimes should not emit anything further.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for close/unsubscribe semantics, and the excerpt has no assertion that event listeners are cleared on close.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a runtime, register both subscribe() and subscribeEvents() listeners, call close(), then apply a user-visible action such as stop() or a backend event and assert neither listener fires and both listener sets are released through public behavior.
minimumFixScope: ConversationRuntime.close() and focused runtime close/unsubscribe tests.
